tagline: Leading manufacturer of metal cutting tools and infrastructure solutions for aerospace, energy, and industrial markets
hero_kpi_rationale: The Infrastructure segment saw its operating margin surge from 5.2% to 7.8% in one year, driven by efficiency gains and strategic projects in energy and public works, becoming the profitability engine despite Metal Cutting weakness.

kpis.name: Infrastructure Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Profitability of the Infrastructure segment, which includes energy and public works.
kpis.description: The Infrastructure segment operating margin rose from 5.2% in 2024 to 7.8% in 2025, supported by productivity gains, restructurings, and high-value-added projects in energy.
kpis.signal: Margin up sharply despite lower sales: sign of operational discipline.

kpis.name: Metal Cutting Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Profitability of the core Metal Cutting segment, which manufactures cutting tools.
kpis.description: The Metal Cutting segment operating margin declined from 10.4% in 2024 to 7.1% in 2025 due to lower volumes, wage inflation, and tariffs.
kpis.signal: Sharp margin decline on core business.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue declined 4% in 2025 to $1,967M ($1.967B), pressured by 4% organic decline and negative currency effects.
kpis.signal: Modest contraction after an already difficult year.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin declined from 30.6% in 2024 to 30.4% in 2025, affected by volumes and currencies, but supported by raw material cost savings.

kpis.name: Research and Development (% of Revenue)
kpis.description: R&D spending reached $44.4M in 2025, or 2.3% of revenue, stable versus 2024, with focus on product innovation.
kpis.signal: Modest R&D level for tech sector, but consistent with industrials.

kpis.name: Annual Restructuring Savings
kpis.explanation: Recurring savings generated by cost reduction programs.
kpis.description: Restructuring actions generated $35M in savings in 2024 and an additional $28M in 2025, totaling $63M in annual run-rate gains.
kpis.signal: Over $60M in annual savings realized in 2025, exceeding targets.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.description: The company closed sites in the United States (Greenfield, MA) and Spain (Barcelona) in 2025. Exact employee count not provided in 10-K excerpts.
kpis.signal: Implicit reduction via plant closures (Greenfield, Barcelona) in 2025.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of $2.55B in latest year

kpis.name: Infrastructure Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Profit generated by the Infrastructure segment.
kpis.description: Infrastructure operating income jumped from $39.9M in 2024 to $58.5M in 2025, driven by efficiency gains, IRA tax credits, and strategic projects.
kpis.signal: Strong income growth despite lower sales.

kpis.name: Metal Cutting Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Profit generated by the company's core segment.
kpis.description: Metal Cutting operating income declined from $132.6M in 2024 to $86.4M in 2025 due to lower volumes, wage inflation, and tariffs.
kpis.signal: Sharp drop in operating income on core business.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du résultat net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence, generative AI, or machine learning solutions in the provided documents. Innovation is centered on advanced manufacturing, materials, and operational efficiency.
evidence: No reference to AI or intelligent automation in segments or products
R&D investments described as focused on product quality, not software or AI
Productivity gains stem from restructurings and IRA tax credits, not digitalization or AI
